title: Bulgur vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Bulgur vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g cooked, bulgur has about 83 calories and 4.5 g fiber; couscous about 112 calories and 1.4 g fiber. Both contain gluten.
seo.search_intent: Compare bulgur and couscous for fiber, protein, calories, processing, and gluten.

excerpt: Cooked bulgur usually has fewer calories and much more fiber than refined couscous: about 83 calories and 4.5 g fiber per 100 g versus 112 calories and 1.4 g. Both come from wheat and contain gluten, but bulgur is typically a whole-grain product.
content_html:
Bulgur and couscous can fill the same space in a salad or side dish, but they are not the same wheat product. Bulgur is whole wheat that has been parboiled, dried, and cracked; traditional couscous is made from tiny granules of durum-wheat semolina, usually refined. That processing difference explains bulgur's clearest nutritional advantage: much more fiber.

Per 100 g cooked

BulgurRefined couscous
Calories~83~112
Protein~3.1 g~3.8 g
Fiber~4.5 g~1.4 g

Couscous has only about 0.7 g more protein per 100 g cooked. Bulgur, by contrast, provides about 3.1 g more fiber—a little over three times as much as refined couscous.

In a 180 g cooked serving, that is roughly 8.1 g fiber from bulgur versus 2.5 g from couscous. That gap is large enough to matter in an ordinary meal.

Why bulgur keeps more fiber

Bulgur begins as whole wheat and retains the bran, germ, and endosperm in whole-grain proportions. Conventional couscous usually starts with refined semolina, so much of the bran and germ have already been removed.

Whole-wheat couscous also exists. It can narrow the fiber gap substantially, which is why the actual ingredient list matters more than assuming all couscous has one nutritional profile.

The calorie gap partly reflects water

The reference values put cooked bulgur around 83 calories per 100 g and couscous around 112. Part of that difference reflects final hydration: more water in the cooked food dilutes calories per 100 g. Bulgur has not somehow destroyed calories during cooking.

Both contain gluten

Both foods are wheat products. Someone with celiac disease or another reason to avoid gluten needs a different base, such as rice, quinoa, corn, or appropriately certified buckwheat.

Cooking speed is closer than it looks

Instant couscous can hydrate in a few minutes. Fine bulgur can also be very quick, while coarse bulgur takes longer and gives a firmer, chewier result.

The practical choice

Choose bulgur when fiber and a whole-grain texture matter most. Choose couscous when you want an especially light texture and near-instant preparation. Protein is too close to be a useful deciding factor.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Cooked bulgur, about 4.5 g/100 g versus roughly 1.4 g/100 g in refined couscous.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Couscous can have a small cooked-weight advantage, around 3.8 g/100 g versus about 3.1 g.

faq.question: Do both contain gluten?
faq.answer: Yes. Both are made from wheat.
